purpose: Ability-package reprint review. Preserve identity, art and rarity; costs and bodies account for the revised abilities. Basic Wellsprings deliberately retain the shared resource rule.

SF002-002.reason: The moth carries its last seed to another living guardian.

SF002-005.reason: Shelter earns a small delayed recovery; one less immediate guard.

SF002-006.reason: The small ground Intercept creature needs to survive a one-damage exchange.

SF002-007.reason: The courier delivers a final restorative parcel.

SF002-008.reason: A three-cost restorative ground creature needs enough attack to contribute when no ally is wounded.

SF002-010.reason: The four-cost ground grazer supports Verdance's slower mixed curves and leaves a small reserve of sustenance.

SF002-012.reason: The ape clears a small blocker at arrival; loses one guard.

SF002-045.reason: Breaking the fragile coal shell releases its ember.

SF002-047.reason: An oathling must survive its charge to finish its promise.

SF002-048.reason: The porter's final act shields the evacuation.

SF002-051.reason: A falling scavenger scatters a final ember; its body supports Pyre's fragile tempo curve.

SF002-053.reason: Its banked slag powers one later turn, once per entry.

SF002-055.reason: The five-cost charging flyer needs meaningful pressure to finish a fragile tempo curve.

SF002-056.reason: The surviving custodian opens a furnace record and releases its banked heat.

SF002-064.reason: The last furnace wave leaves a little heat for another spell.

SF002-066.reason: Riskier, sturdier salvaging than an old unconditional draw body.

SF002-068.reason: The basilisk's first furnace gaze sears its foe.

SF002-088.reason: The drifter's glassfin releases a restorative pearl.

SF002-090.reason: Listening finds a safe resource route rather than raw card draw.

SF002-092.reason: A small immediate recovery, with testimony recovered only on death.

SF002-093.reason: A fragile scout marks a supply route if it survives.

SF002-095.reason: The memory must be protected before its card arrives.

SF002-096.reason: The breakwater must weather a turn to earn its shell's full size.

SF002-098.reason: A less durable flyer leaves a recovered fast-response spell.

SF002-104.reason: Borrowed currents find supplies rather than unrestricted card cycling.

SF002-106.reason: One unknown memory and one resource route replace a raw Draw 2 reprint.

SF002-107.reason: A fast cantrip should not also remove the typical three-guard unit at full rate; Tide retains recall as its main tempo tool.

SF002-108.reason: The cheap recall has a tangible health cost.

SF002-110.reason: Distinct restorative reserves without repeating the forest medic.

SF002-112.reason: A less durable bailiff earns a small recovery by holding its post.

SF002-116.reason: Refusing the spell returns a little vitality to its caster.

SF002-118.reason: A recovery ritual, with less unrestricted draw and wounded-board support.

SF002-120.reason: Recall plus a delayed card should leave a removable midgame body.

SF002-121.reason: The temporal watch leaves recovery, with a smaller evasive body.

SF002-122.reason: Half the testament is answerable before it becomes card advantage.

SF002-127.reason: The intercepting recall body already provides tempo and protection; reduce accumulated free value.

SF002-128.reason: The delayed mass recall must have a practical removal window.

SF002-129.reason: The evasive life-gain and card-advantage finisher needs a less durable body.

SF002-132.reason: A fragile recruit earns recovery by surviving its first watch.

SF002-134.reason: The broken guardian leaves its watch-lantern active.

SF002-135.reason: The falcon delivers a mending banner to a wounded ally.

SF002-137.reason: A kept watch strengthens its attendant and restores the refuge.

SF002-138.reason: The candle remains lit only if the scribe survives.

SF002-139.reason: The defender's departing light protects its commander.

SF002-140.reason: The lancer earns its durability through a surviving watch.

SF002-148.reason: Dawn's recovery cantrip should not remove a three-guard unit as efficiently as Pyre's dedicated damage; retain its defensive identity.

SF002-152.reason: Split recovery for a wounded ally and its commander.

SF002-153.reason: Early Aegis plus delayed life gain must remain answerable by ordinary removal in mixed-set decks.

SF002-163.reason: Immediate four-health recovery and army-wide permanent growth already provide value; reduce the body protecting that mixed-set payoff.

SF002-164.reason: Evasive first-strike pressure needs the same three-damage removal window as comparable five-cost flyers.

SF002-168.reason: Permanent army-wide growth plus three immediately strengthened Alert tokens needs a six-Aether commitment, especially with original-set armies. Preserve the three lanterns depicted by its art.

SF002-170.reason: The Alert and Aegis army leader needs a practical combat removal window before its growth and recovery payoff.

SF002-171.reason: An Alert finisher with immediate recovery and two delayed cards needs a less durable body.

SF002-175.reason: The fragile secret-carrier pays life for its surviving testimony.

SF002-177.reason: Destroying the watcher also destroys an opponent's secret.

SF002-178.reason: The small leeching bat leaves a final drop of stolen vitality.

SF002-180.reason: A surviving oathhound finishes one small drain.

SF002-181.reason: A mourner pays for the memory now and returns it on death.

SF002-183.reason: A slow drain guardian needs to survive ordinary midgame attacks to earn its Vow.

SF002-184.reason: The grief vessel breaks into a lingering echo and a moment of relief.

SF002-191.reason: Exchange secrets at a life cost rather than duplicate the old draw ritual.

SF002-197.reason: Support Gloom's delayed pressure in both mixed and expansion value decks.
